expectations.text: Keeps one resource per API service and prefers many small resources over one holding a whole account.
expectations.evidence: Section 5 maps each API object to its own small resource: workspace, workspace_member, team_member, template, segment and sending_domain. Push-back 1 drops the inline members block on marrowgate_workspace in favour of a separate attachment resource, and push-back 2 refuses a separate state resource because it would fight template over one field. Nothing in the design bundles a whole account into one resource. The transcript never states the rule against an account-wide mega-resource outright, so the preference has to be inferred from the design. The score is held below 5 for that reason.

expectations.text: Keeps one resource per API service and prefers many small resources over one holding a whole account.
expectations.evidence: The proposed v1 scope splits the API into small, separate resources: `marrowgate_workspace`, `marrowgate_workspace_member`, `marrowgate_template`, `marrowgate_segment` and `marrowgate_account_sending_domain`. Pushback 2 rejects inline `members` on the workspace in favour of a separate `workspace_member` resource. It also defers an authoritative `workspace_members` resource. Pushback 3 avoids one resource fighting another over the same object. These choices follow the principle in practice.
